notes: Add 'po' with vendors older than you. 'Magkano lahat?' = how much all together.

examples.tl: Magkano po ito? — Dalawang daan lang po.
examples.en: How much is this? — Just two hundred.

notes: For palengke, tiangge, Divisoria, Greenhills. Not for malls or restaurants. Root tawad = discount/haggle.

examples.tl: Pwede bang tumawad, ate? — Sige, bawas ko ng bente.
examples.en: Can I haggle, miss? — Okay, I'll take off twenty.

notes: Pattern: 'Meron ba kayong ...?' for anything in a store or restaurant. 'Mayroon' is the full form; 'meron' is what you'll hear.

examples.tl: Meron ba kayong extra rice? — Meron po.
examples.en: Do you have extra rice? — Yes, we do.

notes: CR = comfort room, universal in Manila. 'Banyo' is bathroom at home.

examples.tl: Saan po ang CR? — Diyan po sa likod, kanan.
examples.en: Where's the restroom? — Back there, to the right.

notes: 'Pahingi ng ...' is the most natural way to ask for something at a table. Paki- + root = 'please do X'.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng tubig. — Service water or bottled?
examples.en: Can I have some water, please? — Service water or bottled?

notes: 'Dalawang order ng ...' for two. Carinderia style: point and say 'Isa nito.'

examples.tl: Isang order ng sisig at dalawang kanin. — Sige po, dine-in?
examples.en: One order of sisig and two rice. — Okay, dine-in?

notes: Usual question is 'Ilan po kayo?' (How many are you?). Answer 'Dalawa po.'

examples.tl: Ilan po kayo? — Para sa dalawa po.
examples.en: How many are you? — For two.

notes: Opposite: 'Dine-in po.' Nobody says 'to go' in Manila.

examples.tl: Dine-in or take-out po? — Take-out po.
examples.en: Dine-in or take-out? — Take-out, please.

notes: Sari-sari store opener. 'Pabili ng ...' = let me buy some ... Also 'Pabili po!' to call the tindera.

examples.tl: Ate, pabili ng tubig. — Malamig o hindi?
examples.en: Miss, I'd like to buy water. — Cold or not?

notes: Drivers and tinderas ask 'May barya ka?' or 'Wala kang barya?'. 'Maliit' = small bills.

examples.tl: Wala po akong barya, isang libo lang. — Ay, wala akong panukli.
examples.en: I don't have change, only a thousand. — Oh, I don't have change for that.

notes: Also 'Pwede card?' / 'Cash only po?'. Many small stalls have a GCash QR taped up.

examples.tl: Pwede GCash? — Pwede po, i-scan niyo lang yung QR.
examples.en: Can I pay with GCash? — Yes, just scan the QR.

notes: 'Bill out' is the everyday Taglish verb. 'Chit' is older but still understood. Hand signal: write in the air.

examples.tl: Yung bill po. — Sige po, isang bill lang?
examples.en: The bill, please. — Sure, just one bill?

notes: Answer to a driver's 'Saan po tayo?' (Where to?). Add a landmark: 'Sa Makati po, malapit sa Greenbelt.'

examples.tl: Saan po tayo? — Sa Makati po, Ayala Avenue.
examples.en: Where to? — Makati, Ayala Avenue.

notes: Tells a driver to drop you here. On a jeep shout 'Para po!' instead.

examples.tl: Saan po kayo bababa? — Dito lang po, sa tabi.
examples.en: Where will you get off? — Just here, on the side.

notes: 'Para!' (from Spanish parar) is the jeep/bus word; 'pakihinto' is fine for a car or Grab.

examples.tl: Kuya, pakihinto dito sa kanto. — Sige po.
examples.en: Sir, please stop here at the corner. — Okay.

notes: Spelled diretso or deretso. Directions you'll hear: diretso, kaliwa, kanan, U-turn, sa kanto.

examples.tl: Kaliwa po ba dito? — Hindi, diretso lang, tapos kanan.
examples.en: Left here? — No, just go straight, then right.

notes: Kanan = right. 'Sa susunod na kanto' = at the next corner.

examples.tl: Kaliwa sa kanto, tapos dito lang po. — Okay.
examples.en: Left at the corner, then just here. — Okay.

accept: Turn right at the next corner.
notes: 'Susunod' = next. Also heard: 'Sa unahan, kanan' (up ahead, right).

examples.tl: Saan po? — Kanan sa susunod na kanto, sa may 7-Eleven.
examples.en: Where? — Right at the next corner, by the 7-Eleven.

notes: 'Matagal pa ba?' = is it still a long wait? Useful for food, Grab, and queues.

examples.tl: Gaano katagal yung order? — Mga sampung minuto po.
examples.en: How long for the order? — About ten minutes.

notes: 'Ilang minuto pa?' = how many more minutes. Common reply: 'Lima pa' or 'Malapit na' (almost).

examples.tl: Ilang minuto pa, kuya? — Lima pa po, traffic eh.
examples.en: How many more minutes? — Five more, there's traffic.

accept_tl: Sa inyo na po ang sukli.
notes: Sukli = change (money back). 'Okay na yan' while waving off change also works.

examples.tl: Yung sukli niyo po. — Sa'yo na, kuya, salamat.
examples.en: Here's your change. — Keep it, thanks.

notes: Resibo or receipt, both used. OR = official receipt.

examples.tl: Pahingi po ng resibo. — Eto po.
examples.en: Can I have a receipt? — Here you go.

notes: 'Bestseller' is the word staff use for the recommended dish.

examples.tl: Anong masarap dito? — Yung crispy pata po, bestseller.
examples.en: What's good here? — The crispy pata, it's the bestseller.

notes: Say it while catching the server's eye. Solo: 'Order na ako.'

examples.tl: Order na po kami. — Sige po, ano pong sa inyo?
examples.en: We're ready to order. — Okay, what will you have?

notes: Works for drinks, rice, anything. 'Isa pang San Mig' = one more San Mig.

examples.tl: Isa pa pong kanin. — Sige po.
examples.en: One more rice, please. — Okay.

notes: Open: 'Anong oras kayo nagbubukas?' 'Bukas pa ba kayo?' = are you still open?

examples.tl: Anong oras po kayo nagsasara? — Alas-diyes po ng gabi.
examples.en: What time do you close? — Ten p.m.

en: Do you have a bigger one?
notes: Mas = more. Mas maliit = smaller, mas mura = cheaper, ibang kulay = other color.

examples.tl: May mas malaki po ba nito? — Wala na po, medium na lang.
examples.en: Do you have this in a bigger size? — None left, only medium.

notes: Pinaka- = most, so pinakamalapit = nearest. Swap in ATM, botika (pharmacy), palengke, MRT.

examples.tl: Saan ang pinakamalapit na ATM? — Sa labas lang, sa tabi ng Jollibee.
examples.en: Where's the nearest ATM? — Just outside, next to Jollibee.

en: Where do I catch a ride to BGC?
accept: Where do I ride to BGC?
accept_tl: Saan po ang sakayan papuntang BGC?
Saan ako pwedeng sumakay papuntang BGC?
notes: Sakay = ride/board; sakayan = the stop or terminal. Papunta sa / papuntang = heading to.

examples.tl: Saan po ako sasakay papuntang BGC? — Doon po sa BGC Bus sa may Ayala.
examples.en: Where do I catch a ride to BGC? — Over there at the BGC Bus by Ayala.

notes: 'Ako nga pala si ...' = by the way, I'm ... (natural when you forgot to introduce yourself).

examples.tl: Ako nga pala si Lloyd. — Ako si Jen. Nice to meet you!
examples.en: By the way, I'm Lloyd. — I'm Jen. Nice to meet you!

notes: Taga- + place = from that place. People will often ask 'Kano ka?' (short for Amerikano).

examples.tl: Taga-saan ka? — Taga-Amerika ako, pero dito na ako nakatira.
examples.en: Where are you from? — I'm from America, but I live here now.

notes: Nakatira = lives/resides. Casual: 'Sa Makati ako' is enough in context.

examples.tl: Saan ka nakatira? — Nakatira ako sa Makati, malapit sa Rockwell.
examples.en: Where do you live? — I live in Makati, near Rockwell.

accept: I've been here for two years.
accept_tl: Dalawang taon na ako sa Pilipinas.
Dalawang taon na ako sa Maynila.
notes: 'Na' marks 'already/by now'. Numbers in English are common in Taglish: 'Three years na ako dito.'

examples.tl: Gaano ka na katagal dito? — Dalawang taon na ako dito.
examples.en: How long have you been here? — I've been here two years.

notes: Expect the reply 'Ay, magaling!' (wow, good!) and then a Tagalog quiz.

examples.tl: Marunong ka mag-Tagalog? — Nag-aaral pa ako ng Tagalog. Konti lang.
examples.en: Can you speak Tagalog? — I'm still learning Tagalog. Just a little.

notes: Konti is the spoken form of kaunti. Say it with a smile; it invites people to slow down.

examples.tl: Wow, Tagalog ka! — Konti lang ang alam ko, pakibagalan.
examples.en: Wow, you speak Tagalog! — I only know a little, please go slow.

accept: I used to be a soldier.
notes: Dating = former. 'Beterano' is understood but evokes WWII vets; 'retired military' or 'ex-military' is what people actually say.

examples.tl: Anong trabaho mo dati? — Dating sundalo ako, retired na.
examples.en: What did you do before? — I was a soldier, retired now.

notes: Kumusta and kamusta are both standard. Asking about family is expected small talk, not nosy.

examples.tl: Kumusta ang pamilya mo? — Okay naman, nasa probinsya sila.
examples.en: How's your family? — They're fine, they're in the province.

notes: Asked far more freely than in the US. Answer: 'Kwarenta na ako' or 'Forty na ako.'

examples.tl: Ilang taon ka na? — Trenta'y singko na ako. Ikaw?
examples.en: How old are you? — I'm thirty-five. You?

notes: Saan for 'where' with a verb; nasaan for 'where is' a thing or person.

examples.tl: Saan ka nakatira? — Sa Pasig, pero nagtatrabaho ako sa Makati.
examples.en: Where do you live? — In Pasig, but I work in Makati.

accept: What do you do for work?
notes: 'Work' replaces trabaho in casual Taglish. 'Saan ka nagtatrabaho?' = where do you work.

examples.tl: Anong work mo? — Nasa BPO ako, night shift.
examples.en: What's your job? — I'm in a BPO, night shift.

notes: 'Saan ka galing?' literally asks where you just came from, but is also used for hometown. Expect 'Taga-Batangas ako.'

examples.tl: Taga-saan ka? — Taga-Cebu ako, pero dito na ako nagtatrabaho.
examples.en: Where are you from? — I'm from Cebu, but I work here now.

notes: Standard small talk here, even from strangers. 'Jowa' = boyfriend/girlfriend (slang).

examples.tl: May asawa ka na ba? — Wala pa, single pa ako.
examples.en: Are you married? — Not yet, I'm still single.

notes: 'Pa' = still. Married: 'May asawa na ako.' Divorced/separated: 'Hiwalay na kami.'

examples.tl: May asawa ka na? — Single pa ako. Ikaw?
examples.en: Are you married? — I'm still single. You?

en: How long have you been here?
notes: 'Matagal ka na dito?' = you've been here long? is the most casual version.

examples.tl: Matagal ka na dito? — Oo, two years na.
examples.en: Have you been here long? — Yeah, two years now.

notes: Textbook form; in real life nearly everyone just says 'Nice to meet you.' Saying the Tagalog gets a warm reaction.

examples.tl: Masaya akong makilala ka. — Ako rin! Ingat.
examples.en: Nice to meet you. — Me too! Take care.

notes: Polite to elders: 'Ano pong pangalan ninyo?' With staff just read the name tag and use kuya/ate.

examples.tl: Anong pangalan mo? — Ako si Marco. Ikaw?
examples.en: What's your name? — I'm Marco. You?

tl: Nagpa-practice lang ako ng Tagalog ko.
notes: Nagpa-practice (incompleted) = am practicing. Good answer when someone laughs at your Tagalog, in a friendly way.

examples.tl: Bakit Tagalog ka? — Nagpa-practice lang ako ng Tagalog ko, pasensya na.
examples.en: Why are you speaking Tagalog? — I'm just practicing my Tagalog, sorry.

notes: Gutom (adj) is more common in speech than the verb nagugutom. Reply: 'Kain tayo!'

examples.tl: Gutom na ako. — Ako rin, kain tayo sa labas.
examples.en: I'm hungry. — Me too, let's eat out.

notes: Add 'na' for 'tired now/already'. Haggard = exhausted and looking it (Taglish).

examples.tl: Pagod ako, traffic kanina. — Magpahinga ka muna.
examples.en: I'm tired, there was traffic earlier. — Rest first.

notes: Swap the body part: tiyan (stomach), ngipin (tooth), likod (back), lalamunan (throat).

examples.tl: Masakit ang ulo ko. — May Biogesic ako, gusto mo?
examples.en: I have a headache. — I have Biogesic, want some?

notes: 'Kailangan ko ng ...' + noun. With a verb: 'Kailangan kong umuwi' (I need to go home).

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng tubig, ang init. — Bibili ako sa 7-Eleven.
examples.en: I need water, it's so hot. — I'll buy some at 7-Eleven.

notes: 'Gusto ko ng ...' + noun; 'Gusto kong ...' + verb. 'Gusto mo ng kape?' = want coffee?

examples.tl: Gusto mo ng kape? — Gusto ko ng kape, walang asukal.
examples.en: Want coffee? — I want coffee, no sugar.

notes: Ayoko = ayaw ko, contracted. Soften with 'po' or 'salamat': 'Ayoko po, salamat.' 'Ayoko na' = I've had enough.

examples.tl: Gusto mo pa ng kanin? — Ayoko na, busog na ako.
examples.en: Want more rice? — No more, I'm full.

notes: 'Ewan ko' is more offhand (dunno). 'Ewan' alone can sound dismissive.

examples.tl: Anong oras siya darating? — Hindi ko alam, di pa nag-reply.
examples.en: What time is she arriving? — I don't know, she hasn't replied yet.

notes: 'Gets' (from 'get it') is everyday Taglish: 'Gets mo?' = you get it? 'Gets ko na' = I get it now.

examples.tl: Hindi ko maintindihan, pakiulit. — Ah, sorry. In English: turn left.
examples.en: I don't understand, please repeat. — Oh, sorry. In English: turn left.

notes: 'Ano ulit?' = what again? is the quick casual version. Root ulit = repeat.

examples.tl: Pwede mo bang ulitin? Mabilis masyado. — Sige: sa kanto, kaliwa.
examples.en: Can you repeat that? Too fast. — Sure: at the corner, left.

notes: For speech or a driver. 'Dahan-dahan lang po, kuya' to a speeding Grab driver. Root bagal = slow.

examples.tl: Pakibagalan po, nag-aaral pa ako ng Tagalog. — Ah, sige, dahan-dahan.
examples.en: Please slow down, I'm still learning Tagalog. — Oh, sure, slowly.

notes: 'Okay lang' answers 'Kumusta?' and 'Okay ka lang?' (are you okay?). Lang softens it.

examples.tl: Okay ka lang? Parang pagod ka. — Okay lang ako, puyat lang.
examples.en: Are you okay? You look tired. — I'm okay, just didn't sleep much.

notes: 'Sure' has fully replaced sigurado in casual speech. 'Sure ka?' = are you sure?

examples.tl: Bukas ba ang Sunday? — Hindi ako sigurado, i-check ko.
examples.en: Is it open on Sunday? — I'm not sure, I'll check.

notes: Siguro = maybe/probably; baka = maybe (less sure); malamang = most likely. 'Siguro nga' = yeah, probably.

examples.tl: Uulan ba mamaya? — Siguro, madilim na.
examples.en: Will it rain later? — Maybe, it's already dark.

notes: Mamaya = later today. 'Mamaya na lang' = let's just do it later. Bukas = tomorrow.

examples.tl: Kakain ka na? — Baka mamaya, busog pa ako.
examples.en: Are you eating now? — Maybe later, I'm still full.

notes: Pronounced 'tignan'. Non-committal answer to plans. 'Bahala na' = we'll see what happens / leave it to fate.

examples.tl: Sama ka sa Sabado? — Tingnan natin, may trabaho pa ako.
examples.en: Coming on Saturday? — Let's see, I still have work.

notes: Puyat = sleep-deprived (stayed up late). 'Antok' alone works casually.

examples.tl: Inaantok na ako. — Uwi na tayo, late na rin.
examples.en: I'm sleepy. — Let's head home, it's late anyway.

notes: Uhaw (adj) also works alone, like gutom. 'Uhaw' as slang can mean thirsty for attention, context matters.

examples.tl: Nauuhaw ako. — May tubig sa ref, kuha ka lang.
examples.en: I'm thirsty. — There's water in the fridge, just grab some.

notes: Pakiramdam = feeling. 'May sakit ako' = I'm sick. 'May lagnat ako' = I have a fever.

examples.tl: Masama ang pakiramdam ko. — Uminom ka ng gamot, magpahinga ka.
examples.en: I don't feel well. — Take some medicine, get some rest.

notes: 'Ang + adjective' = exclamation (so X!). Daily conversation starter from March to June. Mainit = hot (plain).

examples.tl: Ang init! — Oo nga, pumasok tayo sa mall, may aircon.
examples.en: It's so hot! — Yeah, let's go in the mall, there's aircon.

en: I need to go home now.
accept_tl: Kailangan ko nang umuwi, late na.
notes: 'Nang' here = 'na' + linker ng. Softer exit: 'Mauna na ako' (I'll go ahead).

examples.tl: Isa pa! — Kailangan ko nang umuwi, may trabaho bukas.
examples.en: One more! — I need to go home now, I have work tomorrow.

notes: Almost everyone in Manila switches without fuss. 'English na lang po' = let's just do English.

examples.tl: Pwede po English? Nag-aaral pa ako. — Sure, no problem!
examples.en: Can we speak English? I'm still learning. — Sure, no problem!

notes: Saglit and teka are equally common. 'Teka' also = 'wait, what?' when surprised.

examples.tl: Tara na! — Sandali lang, kukunin ko lang ang wallet ko.
examples.en: Let's go! — Just a moment, I'll just grab my wallet.

notes: Kaya = able to manage. 'Kaya ko' = I can handle it; 'Kaya mo yan!' = you can do it!

examples.tl: Isa pang shot! — Hindi ko na kaya, sobra na.
examples.en: One more shot! — I can't anymore, that's too much.

accept_tl: Miss ko na ang pamilya ko.
taglish: Miss ko na ang pamilya ko.
notes: Miss is fully borrowed: na-miss (did miss), nami-miss (am missing). 'Miss ko na kayo' = I miss you guys.

examples.tl: Uuwi ka ba sa States sa Pasko? — Oo, miss ko na ang pamilya ko.
examples.en: Going home to the States for Christmas? — Yeah, I miss my family.

notes: Gagawin = will do (contemplated). 'May lakad ka bukas?' = you got plans tomorrow?

examples.tl: Anong gagawin mo bukas? — Wala, free ako. Bakit?
examples.en: What are you doing tomorrow? — Nothing, I'm free. Why?

notes: Tara = come on/let's go. 'Kain tayo' is also the polite thing to say when you're eating and someone walks by.

examples.tl: Tara, kain tayo. — Saan? Gutom na rin ako.
examples.en: Come on, let's eat. — Where? I'm hungry too.

notes: Libre = free/treat. 'Sagot ko' = I've got this (bill). Expect 'Libre mo!' when it's your birthday or payday.

examples.tl: Magkano hati natin? — Wala, libre kita. Birthday ko kahapon.
examples.en: How much is my share? — Nothing, my treat. It was my birthday yesterday.

notes: Kakain = will eat. The usual non-answer: 'Kahit saan' (anywhere) or 'Ikaw bahala.'

examples.tl: Saan tayo kakain? — Sa Poblacion, may bago doon.
examples.en: Where should we eat? — In Poblacion, there's a new place there.

notes: Magkikita = will see each other. Reply: 'Mga alas-siyete' (around seven) or '7 pm, Filipino time' (meaning late).

examples.tl: Anong oras tayo magkikita? — Mga alas-sais, sa Greenbelt.
examples.en: What time are we meeting? — Around six, at Greenbelt.

notes: 'Sa' + day = on that day. 'Na lang' = let's just... (settling on something).

examples.tl: Busy ako ngayong linggo. — Sige, sa Sabado tayo.
examples.en: I'm busy this week. — Okay, let's do Saturday.

notes: Linggo (capital) = Sunday; linggo = week. 'Pwede ba sa ...?' works for any day or time.

examples.tl: Pwede ba sa Linggo? — Pwede, after mass.
examples.en: Can we do Sunday? — Sure, after mass.

notes: Lakad literally = walk, but 'may lakad' = have an errand/outing/plans. Polite way to decline without details.

examples.tl: Sama ka mamaya? — Sorry, may lakad ako. Next time.
examples.en: Coming later? — Sorry, I have plans. Next time.

notes: 'Abala' is the Tagalog word but 'busy' is what everyone says. 'Eh' at the end softens it as an excuse.

examples.tl: Pwede ka ba ngayon? — Busy ako ngayon, eh. Mamaya na lang?
examples.en: Are you free now? — I'm busy right now. Later instead?

notes: Tapos = finished; also 'then/after that' in storytelling. 'Tapos ka na?' = are you done?

examples.tl: Tapos ka na sa gym? — Tapos na ako, papunta na sa'yo.
examples.en: Done at the gym? — I'm done, heading to you now.

notes: 'Otw' is the standard text. 'Paalis na ako' = just leaving. Everyone knows 'papunta na' often means 'still in the shower'.

examples.tl: Asan ka na? — Papunta na ako, 10 minutes.
examples.en: Where are you? — I'm on my way, 10 minutes.

notes: Means 'out of the house' or 'right outside the door' depending on context. 'Nasa bahay ako' = I'm home.

examples.tl: Nasa unit ka ba? — Hindi, nasa labas ako, balik ako mamaya.
examples.en: Are you in your unit? — No, I'm out, I'll be back later.

notes: Andito/nandito/narito all = here. Baba = down/below. Text this to a friend or a Grab driver from the lobby.

examples.tl: Andito na ako sa baba. — Sige, bababa na ako.
examples.en: I'm downstairs now. — Okay, I'm coming down.

notes: Antayin is the spoken variant of hintayin. 'Hintay' alone = wait up.

examples.tl: Hintayin mo ako sa labas. — Sige, dito lang ako sa gate.
examples.en: Wait for me outside. — Okay, I'll be right here by the gate.

notes: Kita = I...you. Sundo = pick-up; 'May sundo ka?' = is someone picking you up? 'Hatid-sundo' = drop-off and pick-up.

examples.tl: Paano ako pupunta doon? — Sunduin kita, 6 pm sa lobby.
examples.en: How do I get there? — I'll pick you up, 6 pm at the lobby.

notes: Hatid = escort/bring someone somewhere. Normal courtesy after a night out: 'Hatid na kita' = let me take you home.

examples.tl: Late na, paano ka uuwi? — Okay lang. — Ihahatid kita, malapit lang.
examples.en: It's late, how are you getting home? — I'm fine. — I'll take you home, it's close.

notes: Game = willing/up for it. 'G' is the text version. 'Game ka?' = you in?

examples.tl: Inuman mamaya, game ka? — Game ako, anong oras?
examples.en: Drinks later, you in? — I'm in, what time?

notes: Polite decline. 'Ha?' at the end = okay? Sa susunod = next time (Tagalog).

examples.tl: Sama ka sa Tagaytay? — Next time na lang, may trabaho ako.
examples.en: Coming to Tagaytay? — Maybe next time, I have work.

notes: Male-late (will be late), na-late (was late). Universal excuse: 'kasi traffic'.

examples.tl: Male-late ako ng konti, traffic sa EDSA. — Okay, order na muna ako.
examples.en: I'll be a little late, traffic on EDSA. — Okay, I'll order first.

notes: 'Asan ka na?' is the text version. Nasaan for location of a person or thing; saan with verbs.

examples.tl: Nasaan ka na? — Nasa Grab na ako, 5 minutes.
examples.en: Where are you now? — I'm in the Grab, 5 minutes.

notes: 'Kita-kits' is playful. 'Kita tayo mamaya' = see you later.

examples.tl: Sige, kita tayo bukas. — Sige, ingat!
examples.en: Okay, see you tomorrow. — Okay, take care!

notes: 'Uwi na ako' (casual) and 'Uuwi na ako' (proper future) both fine. 'Pauwi na ako' = on my way home.

examples.tl: Uwi na ako, late na. — Sige, text mo ako pag nakauwi ka.
examples.en: I'm heading home, it's late. — Okay, text me when you get home.

accept_tl: Mag-book na lang tayo ng Grab.
notes: Mag- + brand = use that service: mag-Grab, mag-GCash, mag-jeep, mag-MRT.

examples.tl: Ang hirap mag-taxi dito. — Mag-Grab na lang tayo, ako na mag-book.
examples.en: It's hard to get a taxi here. — Let's just take a Grab, I'll book.

notes: KKB = kanya-kanyang bayad (each pays their own), said as letters 'ka-ka-bi'. 'Hati tayo' = let's split.

examples.tl: Sagot mo ba 'to? — Hindi, KKB tayo ngayon, petsa de peligro.
examples.en: Is this on you? — No, we split today, it's the broke days before payday.

notes: Saklolo is the old emergency word, rarely heard now. Tulong is both the noun 'help' and the shout.

examples.tl: Tulong! May nahulog! — Tawag ka ng guard!
examples.en: Help! Someone fell! — Call the guard!

notes: 'Patulong po' is the quick polite version with staff or strangers. Tulungan = help (object focus).

examples.tl: Pwede mo ba akong tulungan? Nawawala ako. — Sige, saan ka pupunta?
examples.en: Can you help me? I'm lost. — Sure, where are you going?

notes: Naliligaw (lost one's way) is the precise word; nawawala (missing) is also used for people. 'Ligaw' also = courting.

examples.tl: Nawawala ako, saan ang MRT? — Doon po, diretso lang, kaliwa.
examples.en: I'm lost, where's the MRT? — Over there, just straight, then left.

notes: Nawala (got lost, done) vs nawawala (is missing right now). Pitaka = wallet, but 'wallet' is more common.

examples.tl: Nawala ang wallet ko sa Grab! — Tawagan mo yung driver sa app.
examples.en: I lost my wallet in the Grab! — Call the driver through the app.

accept_tl: Sira po ang aircon sa unit ko.
notes: Sira = broken. 'Aircon' never 'AC' in speech. 'Hindi lumalamig' = it's not getting cold.

examples.tl: Sira ang aircon sa unit ko. — Pakireport sa admin, tatawag sila ng technician.
examples.en: The aircon in my unit is broken. — Report it to admin, they'll call a technician.

notes: 'Walang ...' = there's no ... Gripo = faucet. Ask 'Hanggang kailan?' (until when?).

examples.tl: Walang tubig sa unit ko. — May water interruption po hanggang alas-tres.
examples.en: There's no water in my unit. — There's a water interruption until three.

notes: 'Brownout' means any power outage in the Philippines, not a partial one. 'Walang ilaw' is also used.

examples.tl: Walang kuryente sa floor namin. — Brownout sa buong building, may generator naman.
examples.en: There's no electricity on our floor. — Outage in the whole building, but there's a generator.

notes: Signal = mobile data/reception. Mabagal = slow. 'Anong password ng wifi?' = what's the wifi password?

examples.tl: Walang wifi, hindi ako makapag-work. — I-restart mo yung router.
examples.en: There's no wifi, I can't work. — Restart the router.

notes: Tawagan = call (object focus). 'Tatawag ako' = I'll call. 'Missed call mo ako' = give me a missed call.

examples.tl: Tawagan mo ako pag nandito ka na. — Sige, tawag ako pag nasa lobby na.
examples.en: Call me when you're here. — Okay, I'll call when I'm in the lobby.

notes: I- prefix makes a borrowed verb: i-text, i-send, i-book. 'Chat mo ako' = message me on Messenger/Viber.

examples.tl: I-text mo ako ng address. — Sige, i-send ko yung pin sa Viber.
examples.en: Text me the address. — Okay, I'll send the pin on Viber.

notes: Phone numbers are read in English. 'Globe ka o Smart?' may follow (network for cheaper calls).

examples.tl: Anong number mo? — 0917... i-save mo, Marco.
examples.en: What's your number? — 0917... save it as Marco.

tl: Pakisabi kay Ana na tatawag ako.
accept: Please tell Ana that I will call.
accept_tl: Sabihin mo kay Ana na tatawag ako.
Pakisabi po kay Ana, tatawag ako.
notes: Pattern: 'Pakisabi kay [name] na [message]'. Kay before a person's name; sa before a place or role.

examples.tl: Pakisabi kay Ana na tatawag ako mamaya. — Sige po, sasabihin ko.
examples.en: Please tell Ana I'll call later. — Okay, I'll tell her.

notes: 'May problema ba?' = is there a problem? 'Anong problema?' = what's wrong?

examples.tl: May problema sa order ko, kulang ng isa. — Ay, sorry po, i-check ko.
examples.en: There's a problem with my order, one is missing. — Oh, sorry, I'll check.

notes: Ayos = in order/fine. 'Ayos na ba?' = is it fixed? Also 'Ayos!' = nice!

examples.tl: Kumusta yung aircon? — Ayos na, naayos ng maintenance kanina.
examples.en: How's the aircon? — Fixed now, maintenance fixed it earlier.

notes: Both the reassurance and the response to thanks. 'Wala yun' = that was nothing.

examples.tl: Sorry, na-late ako. — Walang problema, kakadating ko lang din.
examples.en: Sorry, I was late. — No problem, I just got here too.

notes: Gumagana = functions. 'Ayaw gumana' = it refuses to work (very common phrasing). 'Gumagana na' = it works now.

examples.tl: Hindi gumagana yung card ko sa ATM. — Try mo yung ibang machine.
examples.en: My card isn't working at the ATM. — Try the other machine.

notes: Ospital or hospital, both used. ER is 'emergency' or 'ER'. Botika = pharmacy (Mercury Drug, Watsons).

examples.tl: Kailangan ko ng doktor, masama ang pakiramdam ko. — May clinic sa second floor.
examples.en: I need a doctor, I don't feel well. — There's a clinic on the second floor.

notes: 'Traffic' is a noun, adjective and excuse. 'Na-traffic ako' = I got caught in traffic.

examples.tl: Asan ka na? — Na-stuck ako sa traffic sa EDSA, sorry.
examples.en: Where are you? — I'm stuck in traffic on EDSA, sorry.

accept_tl: Naiwan ko yung phone ko sa Grab.
notes: Naiwan = left behind (accidentally). Cellphone or CP in older usage; 'phone' now.

examples.tl: Naiwan ko ang phone ko sa unit. — Balik ka muna, hintayin ka namin.
examples.en: I left my phone in the unit. — Go back first, we'll wait for you.

notes: Load = prepaid credit. 'Pa-load' at any sari-sari store. 'Wala akong data' if on wifi only.

examples.tl: Bakit di ka nag-reply? — Wala akong load, nag-wifi lang ako ngayon.
examples.en: Why didn't you reply? — I had no load, I'm just on wifi now.

notes: Lowbat (low battery) is a full-fledged Filipino word; also jokingly 'I'm drained'. Charger = charger, pahiram = lend me.

examples.tl: Lowbat na ako, pahiram ng charger. — Eto, Type-C ba?
examples.en: My phone's dying, lend me a charger. — Here, is it Type-C?

accept_tl: May wifi po ba? Anong password?
notes: Standard café question. Reply usually points to a sign or the receipt.

examples.tl: Anong password ng wifi? — Nasa resibo po, sa baba.
examples.en: What's the wifi password? — It's on the receipt, at the bottom.

notes: Say it to the cook or tita and you'll be fed more. 'Masarap ba?' = is it good? Opposite: 'Hindi masarap' (never 'pangit' for food).

examples.tl: Masarap ba? — Masarap! Ano 'to? — Sinigang na baboy.
examples.en: Is it good? — Delicious! What is this? — Pork sinigang.

notes: Naman adds a mild complaint. Mahal also = love/dear; context makes it clear. Opposite: mura (cheap).

examples.tl: Tatlong libo po. — Ang mahal naman! Pwede bang tumawad?
examples.en: Three thousand. — That's so expensive! Can I haggle?

notes: Sulit = you got your money's worth. 'Sulit na sulit' = totally worth it. 'Hindi sulit' = not worth it.

examples.tl: Unli samgyup, 499 lang. — Sulit! Tara.
examples.en: Unlimited samgyupsal, only 499. — Worth it! Let's go.

notes: Covers missed chances, wasted food, a near-miss shot. 'Sayang ang pagkain' = don't waste the food.

examples.tl: Sold out na yung tickets. — Sayang! Next time na lang.
examples.en: The tickets are sold out. — Too bad! Maybe next time.

notes: For places, views, things, and people. 'Ang ganda ng view' = the view is beautiful. Gwapo for handsome.

examples.tl: Ang ganda ng view dito sa rooftop. — Oo nga, lalo na pag sunset.
examples.en: The view here on the rooftop is beautiful. — Yeah, especially at sunset.

notes: Approval for a plan, a purchase, a result. 'Ayos ba?' = good? Also 'Ayos lang' = it's fine.

examples.tl: Nakakuha ako ng unit malapit sa MRT. — Ayos yan, walang traffic.
examples.en: I got a unit near the MRT. — That's good, no traffic.

notes: Tama = correct. 'Korek ka d'yan' is a jokey old-school version. 'Tama!' alone = right!

examples.tl: Mas mura mag-Grab kung dalawa tayo. — Tama ka, hati tayo.
examples.en: It's cheaper to Grab if there are two of us. — You're right, let's split it.

notes: Sang-ayon is formal/written (news, debates). In conversation people say 'Di ako agree' or just 'Hindi, eh'. Direct disagreement is often softened.

examples.tl: Mas masarap ang Jollibee kaysa McDo. — Hindi ako sang-ayon, pero okay yung Chickenjoy.
examples.en: Jollibee is better than McDo. — I disagree, but the Chickenjoy is okay.

notes: Pareho = same/alike. 'Pareho pala tayo' = oh, we're the same (surprise). Friendship starter.

examples.tl: Ayoko ng maanghang. — Pareho tayo, di ko kaya ang Bicol Express.
examples.en: I don't like spicy. — Same here, I can't handle Bicol Express.

notes: Rule: rin after a vowel, din after a consonant, but speakers mix them freely. Negative: 'Ako rin hindi' (me neither).

examples.tl: Gutom na ako. — Ako rin, kain tayo.
examples.en: I'm hungry. — Me too, let's eat.

notes: Bounce any question back. 'Eh ikaw?' is the chatty form. Polite plural: 'Kayo?'

examples.tl: Okay lang ako, pagod lang. Ikaw? — Ayos lang, galing gym.
examples.en: I'm fine, just tired. And you? — Fine, just came from the gym.

notes: Totoo = true/real. 'Totoo ba?' = is it true? 'Hindi totoo yan' = that's not true.

examples.tl: Mas mahal sa BGC kaysa Makati. — Totoo yan, lalo na ang kape.
examples.en: BGC is pricier than Makati. — That's true, especially coffee.

notes: From Spanish siempre. Spelled siyempre/syempre. 'Oo naman' = yes, of course.

examples.tl: Sasama ka sa inuman? — Siyempre, libre mo!
examples.en: You're coming to drinks? — Of course, your treat!

notes: Blunt and dismissive, can sound rude. For 'I'm fine either way' use 'Okay lang sa akin'. 'Pakialamero' = nosy person.

examples.tl: Galit sa'yo si Marco. — Wala akong pakialam, siya ang may kasalanan.
examples.en: Marco is mad at you. — I don't care, he's the one at fault.

notes: Tone decides: warm ('you choose') or dismissive ('whatever, your problem'). 'Ikaw ang bahala' is the safe, friendly version.

examples.tl: Saan tayo kakain? — Ikaw ang bahala, okay lang sa akin.
examples.en: Where should we eat? — You decide, I'm fine with anything.

notes: The neutral 'I don't mind' (vs. 'Wala akong pakialam' which is rude). 'Kahit ano' = anything, 'kahit saan' = anywhere.

examples.tl: Okay ba sa'yo yung Korean? — Okay lang sa akin, kahit ano.
examples.en: Is Korean okay with you? — It's fine with me, anything.

notes: From Spanish grave. All-purpose reaction to anything extreme: traffic, heat, prices, gossip. 'Grabe ka!' = you're too much!

examples.tl: Tatlong oras ako sa EDSA kanina. — Grabe! Bakit di ka nag-MRT?
examples.en: I was on EDSA for three hours earlier. — Wow! Why didn't you take the MRT?

notes: Tagal = long time. 'Ang tagal mo!' = you took forever! (to a late friend). 'Matagal pa?' = still long?

examples.tl: Eto na yung order niyo. — Ang tagal! Isang oras kami naghintay.
examples.en: Here's your order. — That took so long! We waited an hour.

notes: Type = to one's liking, for food, music, or people. 'Trip ko' = I feel like / I'm into. 'Type kita' = I like you.

examples.tl: Gusto mo ng balut? — Hindi ko type, pero try ko.
examples.en: Want some balut? — Not my thing, but I'll try.

notes: Nakaka- + root = causes that feeling: nakakatawa (funny), nakakainis (annoying), nakakapagod (tiring), nakakahiya (embarrassing).

examples.tl: Nakita mo yung meme? — Oo, nakakatawa, totoo pa.
examples.en: Did you see the meme? — Yeah, it's funny, and it's true.

notes: 'Badtrip' = annoyed/bad mood: 'Badtrip ako' or 'Nakaka-badtrip'. 'Inis' = irritation.

examples.tl: Na-cancel ulit yung Grab ko. — Nakakainis, third time na.
examples.en: My Grab got cancelled again. — So annoying, third time already.

notes: Answer to 'Bakit?' or 'Anong meron?'. Also 'Ano yun? — Wala lang' (what was that? — nothing).

examples.tl: Bakit ka nag-Tagalog bigla? — Wala lang, nagpa-practice.
examples.en: Why did you suddenly speak Tagalog? — Nothing, just practicing.

notes: Ganun/ganon = like that (from gayon). 'Ah, ganun' = ah, I see. 'Ganun?' alone = like that?

examples.tl: Closed ang mall bukas, holiday. — Ganun ba? Di ko alam.
examples.en: The mall is closed tomorrow, holiday. — Is that so? I didn't know.

notes: Nga = agreement/emphasis. 'Oo nga, no?' = right? (seeking agreement). 'Oo nga pala' = oh right, that reminds me.

examples.tl: Ang init talaga ngayon. — Oo nga, eh. Grabe.
examples.en: It's really hot today. — Yeah, I know. Crazy.

notes: Pleading 'maybe you could' when asking for a discount or favor, with a smile. Also a mock-reproach: 'Baka naman!' = seriously?

examples.tl: Fixed price po. — Baka naman, kuya, dalawa bibilhin ko.
examples.en: Fixed price. — Come on, man, I'm buying two.

notes: To housekeeping or a kasambahay. Paki-ayos = please tidy. Kwarto = room (bedroom); unit = whole condo.

examples.tl: Ate, pakilinis ng kwarto mamaya, ha? — Sige po, pagkatapos ng banyo.
examples.en: Ate, please clean the room later, okay? — Yes, after the bathroom.

accept_tl: May delivery po para sa akin.
May dadating na delivery para sa akin.
notes: Tell the guard or reception in advance. 'Dadating' = will arrive. Unit number helps: 'Unit 12B po.'

examples.tl: Kuya, may delivery para sa akin mamaya, Unit 12B. — Sige po, tatawagan ko kayo.
examples.en: Kuya, there's a delivery for me later, Unit 12B. — Okay, I'll call you.

accept: Please accept the package for me.
notes: Tanggap = receive/accept. Most condo lobbies log parcels; 'Pakitanggap na lang po' = just receive it for me.

examples.tl: Pakitanggap po ng package ko, wala ako sa unit. — Sige po, i-log namin.
examples.en: Please receive my package, I'm not in the unit. — Okay, we'll log it.

notes: 'Unit' = your condo. 'Nasa taas' = upstairs. Reply when the guard calls about a visitor or delivery.

examples.tl: Sir, nandito po yung rider. — Nasa unit ako, bababa ako.
examples.en: Sir, the rider is here. — I'm in my unit, I'll come down.

notes: Ilaw = light. 'Patay ang ilaw' = the light is off/dead. 'Bukas ang ilaw' = the light is on. Bumbilya = bulb.

examples.tl: Sira ang ilaw sa banyo ko. — Pakireport sa admin, papalitan ng maintenance.
examples.en: The light in my bathroom is broken. — Report it to admin, maintenance will replace it.

notes: 'Patawag' = have someone call. In condos you usually file at the admin office; the guard can relay after hours.

examples.tl: Pakitawag ng maintenance, tumutulo ang gripo. — Sige po, i-report ko sa admin.
examples.en: Please call maintenance, the faucet is leaking. — Okay, I'll report it to admin.

notes: Kuya (older brother) for male guards, drivers, staff; ate for women; 'boss' is also common for men. Add 'po' if older.

examples.tl: Eto po ang package niyo. — Salamat, kuya. Ingat!
examples.en: Here's your package. — Thanks, kuya. Take care!

notes: The standard goodbye. Kayo = plural or polite singular; ka = casual singular. 'Ingat sa daan' = safe trip.

examples.tl: Sige po, uwi na kami. — Sige, ingat kayo!
examples.en: Okay, we're heading home. — Okay, take care!

notes: Baba = down; bababa = will go down. Many condos don't let riders up, so you go down. 'Aakyat ako' = I'll go up.

examples.tl: Sir, nandito na po yung Grab Food niyo. — Sige, bababa ako.
examples.en: Sir, your Grab Food is here. — Okay, I'll come down.

notes: Tell the guard so they can log the visitor. 'Pwede na po siyang umakyat' = they can come up.

examples.tl: May bisita ako mamaya, si Marco. — Sige po, papa-log in namin siya.
examples.en: I have a visitor later, Marco. — Okay, we'll have him log in.

accept_tl: Papuntahin niyo na po sa unit.
notes: Umakyat = go up. Reply when the lobby calls about a visitor. 'Paakyat' = let (them) up.

examples.tl: Sir, may bisita po kayo, si Marco. — Pwede na po siyang umakyat, salamat.
examples.en: Sir, you have a visitor, Marco. — He can come up now, thanks.

notes: Bukas = open (and also 'tomorrow', stress differs: bukás open, búkas tomorrow). 'Pakisara' = please close.

examples.tl: Kuya, pakibukas ng gate, may Grab ako. — Sige po.
examples.en: Kuya, please open the gate, I have a Grab. — Okay.

tl: Pa-deliver po ng tubig, isang galon.
en: Please deliver one gallon of water.
accept: One gallon of water delivered, please.
accept_tl: Pa-refill po ng tubig, isang galon.
Pabili ng isang galon ng tubig.
notes: Water refilling stations deliver 5-gallon containers (called 'galon'). Pa- + verb = have it done for you.

examples.tl: Pa-deliver po ng tubig, isang galon, Unit 12B. — Sige po, 30 minutes.
examples.en: Please deliver one gallon of water, Unit 12B. — Okay, 30 minutes.

tl: Dumating na ba ang package ko?
accept_tl: Andito na ba ang delivery ko?
Nandito na ba ang package ko?
May package po ba para sa Unit 12B?
notes: Dumating = arrived. Ask at the lobby desk; give your unit number. 'Wala pa po' = not yet.

examples.tl: Dumating na ba ang package ko? Unit 12B. — Wala pa po, sir.
examples.en: Has my package arrived? Unit 12B. — Not yet, sir.

notes: For deliveries: tell the guard or rider it's paid online. Opposite: 'COD po' (cash on delivery).

examples.tl: Magkano po babayaran? — Bayad na po, GCash.
examples.en: How much to pay? — It's already paid, GCash.

en: Where do I throw the trash?
notes: Basura = trash, basurahan = bin. Condos have a garbage room per floor or a chute; segregation (nabubulok/di-nabubulok) is often required.

examples.tl: Saan ang tapunan ng basura? — May garbage room sa dulo ng hallway.
examples.en: Where do I throw the trash? — There's a garbage room at the end of the hallway.

notes: Hapon = afternoon, gabi = evening. In Manila 'Good morning po' is more common than the full Tagalog; both are welcome.

examples.tl: Magandang umaga po, kuya. — Magandang umaga po, sir!
examples.en: Good morning, kuya. — Good morning, sir!

notes: Marami = many/much. Po adds respect for elders, staff, strangers. Casual: 'Salamat!' or 'Thanks!'

examples.tl: Eto po ang sukli. — Maraming salamat po.
examples.en: Here's your change. — Thank you very much.

notes: Textbook form; people more often say 'Wala yun' (it's nothing), 'Okay lang', or just smile. Still good to know.

examples.tl: Salamat sa tulong! — Walang anuman, kahit kailan.
examples.en: Thanks for the help! — You're welcome, anytime.

notes: Literally 'patience, please'. The everyday apology for inconvenience: being late, bumping someone, a wrong order. 'Sorry' is also universal.

examples.tl: Pasensya na, na-late ako. — Okay lang, kakadating ko lang din.
examples.en: Sorry about that, I was late. — It's fine, I just got here too.

notes: For squeezing through a crowd, a jeep, or a packed MRT. 'Excuse me po' is also common. 'Daan' = path.

examples.tl: Makikiraan po. — Sige po, dito.
examples.en: Excuse me, coming through. — Sure, here.

notes: 'Kumusta ka na?' = how have you been (haven't seen you in a while). 'Musta?' is text-casual. Also used for 'how was it?': 'Kumusta ang trip?'

examples.tl: Kumusta ka na? — Okay naman, busy lang. Ikaw?
examples.en: How have you been? — Good, just busy. You?

notes: A greeting as much as a question, like 'how are you'. Standard answer: 'Kumain na' or 'Hindi pa'. Often followed by an offer of food.

examples.tl: Kumain ka na ba? — Hindi pa, gutom na nga ako.
examples.en: Have you eaten? — Not yet, I'm actually hungry.

notes: Hindi pa = not yet. Kumakain (incompleted) is the natural form here, not kumain. If you have: 'Kumain na ako.'

examples.tl: Kain ka na? — Hindi pa ako kumakain, tara sa labas.
examples.en: Have you eaten? — I haven't eaten yet, let's go out.

notes: The polite way to leave a group or the office. Reply: 'Sige, ingat!' Una = first/ahead.

examples.tl: Mauna na ako, may lakad pa ako. — Sige, ingat ka!
examples.en: I'll go ahead, I still have plans. — Okay, take care!

notes: Time is answered in English or Spanish-style: 'Alas-tres na' or 'Three na'. 'Anong oras?' with a verb = at what time?

examples.tl: Anong oras na? — Alas-singko na, uwian na.
examples.en: What time is it? — It's five already, time to go home.

notes: Nakalimutan or nalimutan. 'Nakalimutan ko ang password ko' = I forgot my password. 'Wag mong kalimutan' = don't forget.

examples.tl: Dala mo yung ID? — Ay, nakalimutan ko! Nasa unit.
examples.en: Did you bring the ID? — Oh, I forgot! It's in the unit.

notes: Also 'Talaga!' = really/for sure (emphasis). 'Weh?' is playful disbelief among friends. 'Seryoso' from Spanish.

examples.tl: Libre ang kape bukas sa office. — Talaga? Papasok ako nang maaga.
examples.en: Coffee is free at the office tomorrow. — Really? I'll come in early.

notes: Pupunta = will go. 'San ka punta?' is quick casual. Not nosy; a normal greeting in the hallway or elevator.

examples.tl: Saan ka pupunta? — Sa gym lang, tapos grocery.
examples.en: Where are you going? — Just the gym, then groceries.

accept: I just came from the gym.
notes: Galing = came from. Answers 'Saan ka galing?' (where did you come from?). 'Kakagaling ko lang' = I just came from.

examples.tl: Saan ka galing? Pawis ka. — Galing ako sa gym, leg day.
examples.en: Where did you come from? You're sweaty. — I came from the gym, leg day.

notes: Pahiram = let me borrow (pa- + hiram). 'Pahiram ng ballpen/payong/powerbank'. Return: 'Eto na, salamat.'

examples.tl: Pahiram ng charger, lowbat na ako. — Eto, iPhone ba?
examples.en: Can I borrow a charger? My phone's dying. — Here, is it an iPhone?

notes: Called out at a door or gate when there's no doorbell (literally 'a person here!'). Also what a sari-sari store customer shouts.

examples.tl: Tao po! — Sandali lang! Sino yan?
examples.en: Hello, anyone home? — Just a moment! Who is it?

notes: Bawal = forbidden, seen on signs everywhere (Bawal umihi dito). Ask before smoking or taking photos. Opposite: 'Pwede ba dito?'

examples.tl: Bawal ba mag-vape dito? — Bawal po, sa smoking area lang.
examples.en: Is vaping not allowed here? — Not allowed, only in the smoking area.

notes: 'X na lang' = let's just settle on X. Mamaya na lang = later instead. Also used to postpone chores guilt-free.

examples.tl: Gagawin natin ngayon? — Bukas na lang, pagod na ako.
examples.en: Are we doing it now? — Tomorrow instead, I'm tired.

notes: For a crowd, a party, or a traffic jam. 'May meron' (jokey) = there's something going on. 'Anong nangyari?' = what happened?

examples.tl: Anong meron? Ang daming tao. — May sale sa Landmark.
examples.en: What's going on? So many people. — There's a sale at Landmark.
